identity.name: Distarch phosphate
synonyms: Distarch phosphate (esterified with sodium trimetaphosphate or phosphorus oxychloride)
identity.chemical_class: Chemically modified cross-linked starch (phosphate cross-linked starch)

function.mechanism: Chemical cross-linking of food starch chains (e.g., via sodium trimetaphosphate or phosphorus oxychloride) improves process stability and controls viscosity/thickening behavior.

adi.basis: EFSA (2017) concluded no need for a numerical ADI for modified starches including E1412; earlier JECFA/SCF ADI was 'not specified'.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation of modified starches (including E1412) found no safety concern at reported uses and use levels for the general population.

adi.basis: JECFA lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED for distarch phosphate; 2018 entry was specification-only and retained this status.

concerns.summary: An in vitro infant fecal fermentation study using maize hydroxypropylated distarch phosphate reported higher gas production, faster pH drop, and lower microbiota diversity versus locust bean gum in that model.

A 1982 rat study with related modified starches (E1414/E1422, not E1412 directly) reported increased nephrocalcinosis-related findings under test diets, with diet mineral composition discussed as a confounder.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017 re-evaluation found no safety concern for modified starches (including E1412) at reported use levels.
EFSA 2017 reported no genotoxic concern for the modified starch group in the assessment framework.
JECFA retained ADI as NOT SPECIFIED for distarch phosphate.

populations: No numeric ADI applicable (EFSA/JECFA non-numerical ADI framework)
Potential gastrointestinal tolerance attention for high-use infant thickened-food contexts
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported high-percentile grouped exposure for E1404-E1451 up to 3,053 mg/kg bw/day while still concluding no safety concern and no need for a numerical ADI.

risk_assessment.rationale: Major regulators (EFSA, JECFA, FDA framework) continue to permit use, with EFSA/JECFA non-numerical ADI conclusions and no identified IARC classification. Evidence suggesting harm is limited and mainly indirect (in vitro microbiota findings, historical related-modified-starch rat observations).
key_factors: EFSA 2017: no safety concern for modified starches including E1412
JECFA: ADI NOT SPECIFIED retained (latest entry includes 2018 specification-only review)
U.S. use permitted under 21 CFR 172.892 with conditions
No IARC listing identified for distarch phosphate
Direct modern E1412-specific toxicology literature is limited
